name: Porcius
overview: Porcius Festus was a male Roman governor of Caesarea, known for succeeding Felix in this official capacity. His role as governor is noted in the book of Acts, highlighting his administrative authority during the early church period. There is no additional information about his tribe or other personal details.
namesAndTitles: The individual is primarily known as Porcius Festus, with the simpler form 'Festus' also used. Neither name is given by God nor carries a specific Hebrew or Greek meaning in the biblical text, but they identify him as a Roman official mentioned in Acts 24:47 and Acts 25:1.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Porcius Festus beyond his role as governor of Caesarea. There are no known relatives or personal connections documented in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Porcius Festus is significant in the biblical narrative as the successor to Felix as governor of Caesarea. His governance marks a continuation of Roman authority during a critical period of the early church's development. His mention in Acts situates him as an important figure in the legal proceedings involving the Apostle Paul.
